questions.question: Which of these are the four classic types of conflict in fiction?
options: Person vs. person, person vs. self, person vs. nature, person vs. society
Person vs. weather, person vs. food, person vs. time, person vs. money
Hero vs. villain only
Plot vs. theme, setting vs. character
questions.explanation: The four classic conflicts are person vs. person, person vs. self (inner conflict), person vs. nature and person vs. society.

questions.question: Why is "a rainy Tuesday in November" a better setting description than "one day"?
options: It is specific and creates atmosphere with concrete details
It is longer, and longer is always better
It rhymes
It hides information from the reader
questions.explanation: Specific settings with sensory details create atmosphere and pull the reader into the story.

questions.question: Which sentence follows the rule "Show, don't tell"?
options: His hands shook as he tore open the envelope.
He was nervous.
He felt very nervous indeed.
He was extremely nervous about the letter.
questions.explanation: Showing reveals emotions through actions and details ("his hands shook") instead of naming the feeling directly.

questions.question: What is "free verse" in poetry?
options: Poetry without a fixed rhyme scheme or metre
Poetry that is free to download
Poetry with exactly fourteen lines
Poetry that must rhyme in every line
questions.explanation: Free verse follows no fixed rules for rhyme or rhythm, giving the poet freedom in form.

questions.question: What is the "theme" of a story?
options: The message or insight the story conveys
The place where the story happens
The name of the main character
The number of chapters
questions.explanation: The theme is the underlying message or insight, such as friendship, courage or loss - not the plot itself.
